evidence.intree_statement: Definition PreservesAllLimits {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesLimit G F.
Definition PreservesAllColimits {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesColimit G F.
Definition Complete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Limit F.
Definition Cocomplete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F.

statement_record.book: A category is complete (resp. cocomplete) when it has all small limits (resp. all small colimits); a functor is continuous (resp. cocontinuous) when it preserves all small limits (resp. all small colimits).
statement_record.intree: Complete {C} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Limit F;  Cocomplete {C} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F;  PreservesAllLimits F := ∀ J (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesLimit G F;  PreservesAllColimits F := ∀ J (G : J ⟶ C), PreservesColimit G F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with two presentational caveats that are documented in-tree. (1) Smallness: the definitions quantify over ∀ (D : Category) with no explicit smallness predicate; Structure/Complete.v's header states that 'the size discipline is instead carried implicitly by the library's universe polymorphism … the universe-polymorphic stand-in for D small relative to C', so this is the small-limit reading, not the (Freyd-inconsistent) all-diagrams reading. (2) Same-name-but-weaker trap checked: the underlying Class PreservesLimit (Structure/Limit/Preservation.v:48) is APEX-ONLY — 'preserves_limit (L : Limit G) : IsALimit (F ◯ G) (F L)' constrains only the image apex, leaving the legs unconstrained; the cone-level strengthening that Riehl's arguments (e.g. §3.6's use of representability) actually need is PreservesImageLimit (Construction/Comma/Limit.v:110), which is stated separately and is NOT what PreservesAllLimits packages.

verifier.notes: Blind pass reached PRESENT independently. Evidence re-opened and exact: Structure/Complete.v:115 `Definition Complete {C : Category} := forall (D : Category) (F : D --> C), Limit F.` and :119 the Cocomplete dual; Structure/Limit/Preservation.v:229/232 PreservesAllLimits / PreservesAllColimits, quotes verbatim-accurate at those exact lines. All four files registered in _CoqProject. STRENGTHENING THE RECORD (evidence the classifier flagged in prose but did not cite as evidence): the cone-level, faithful reading of Riehl's CONTINUOUS FUNCTOR does exist in-tree as `PreservesImageLimit` (Construction/Comma/Limit.v:110), and after `End CommaLimit` (line 250) it discharges to a fully general `@PreservesImageLimit C D U` over an arbitrary functor U -- see its use at Construction/Comma/Limit.v:265 (`right_adjoint_PreservesImageLimit ... : @PreservesImageLimit C D U`), Adjunction/GAFT.v:242 and Adjunction/SAFT.v:275. So the continuous half is PRESENT in substance, not merely in the apex-only form. TWO HONEST CAVEATS the record understates by opening strength_comparison with 'same': (i) the apex-only `Class PreservesLimit` (Structure/Limit/Preservation.v:48) is STRICTLY weaker than the standard notion -- the library says so itself at Construction/Comma/Limit.v:56-66 -- so `PreservesAllLimits` alone would not have supported a PRESENT verdict; (ii) there is NO named cone-level COCONTINUITY dual: `rg PreservesImage` returns only the limit form, so cocontinuity at cone level is available only by op-ing (`@PreservesImageLimit C^op D^op (F^op)`), consistent with the library's duality-by-definition convention (Colimit F := Limit (F^op)). Classification unchanged.

statement_record.book: If C is complete and cocomplete then so are c/C and C/c: the forgetful functor creates all limits and all connected colimits, and coproducts in c/C are wide pushouts under c (the empty one being id_c).

statement_record.book: In a finitely (co)complete category: the kernel pair (s,t) : R ⇒ X of f is the pullback of f along itself, and (s,t) : R → X × X is monic, hence a relation; kernel pairs are internal equivalence relations (maps ρ, σ, τ satisfying (i)-(iii)); an internal equivalence relation is defined by that data; the coequalizer of s,t is the quotient X/R; and for kernel pairs f factors uniquely as f = m ∘ e through X/R, with m monic in good situations (regular categories, Grothendieck toposes) — the image factorization.
statement_record.intree: regular_factorization f : Factorization f RegularEpiClass MonoClass, built from image_is_coeq (the image is the coequalizer of the kernel pair pullback f f), image_comparison_monic : Monic (image_mor f), and packaged as Regular_OFS : OFS RegularEpiClass MonoClass; Sets_Image_Factorization is the concrete witness in Sets.
